speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe exactly when the swelling and pain in your right ring finger started, and did you have any recent injuries or insect bites?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did you hear or feel a "pop" at the time of injury, and are you able to fully straighten or bend the tip of your finger? I need to check for tendon rupture or a fracture.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text: The inability to actively flex the distal interphalangeal joint with a resting extension strongly suggests a flexor tendon avulsion, likely a Jersey Finger. REQUEST TEST: Ultrasound of right hand.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Ultrasound of the right hand reveals discontinuity of the flexor digitorum profundus (FDP) tendon at its insertion on the distal phalanx of the right ring finger, with proximal retraction of the tendon stump consistent with avulsion injury (Jersey Finger). No significant joint effusion or fracture fragments are visualized.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant medical history. Social history: Student and active in sports, particularly football. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially.
